rust-analyzer|r2_handles|completionResol.evidence: Completion items carry data {position, version: 11, hash} and no textEdit (deferred to resolve, allowed by the client's resolveSupport). After 2 line breaks at the top (version 12), completionItem/resolve of the old item still answers at line 55, where the text now is the previous `buf.extend_from_slice(...)` statement (found again by hash): textEdit and, for the postfix `.arc`/`.rc` items, the deletion of `buf.` land on the wrong line, while a fresh item resolves to line 57. data.version is not checked; codeAction/resolve rejects the same staleness with -32602 'stale code action'.

ts6|r2_handles|completionResolve:changed.evidence: typescript-language-server keeps {file, line, offset, entryNames} per item in completionDataCache (reset only by the next completion request, not by didChange) and completionResolve sends that cached line/offset to tsserver completionEntryDetails. After one line break at the top, the old `count` item is resolved at T0 (311,28), now inside `create(` of the previous statement (a value position): `import { count } from 'node:console'`, while a fresh item at the mapped key position (312,28) resolves to `import type { count } ...`.

Labelled by the checker (differences only in entries wider than the name).

ts7|r3_routes|definitionConsistency.shor.evidence: Object-literal shorthand `{ map, ... }`: the name denotes the property and the variable, so definition there returns both declarations.

After 2 line breaks at the top, the old 'Split elements into separate lines' handle for `grandchildCmd := &Command{...}` (now line 571) splits the composite literal of `rootCmd` (old line 567, now line 569): edits at 569:21/32/43/58 instead of the fresh handle's 571:27/44/55/70.

gopls|r3_routes|highlightVsReferences:ex.evidence: gopls highlights the printf verb that formats the argument under the cursor: on `got` in `t.Fatalf("Expected %q, got %q", expected, got)` the highlight set adds the second `%q` (94:29-31); on `v` in `fmt.Sprintf("Failed to find flag %q ...", v)` it adds `%q` (37:42-44). A format verb is not a reference, so the subset relation fails by design (documented in r3_routes.py).
